test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 6 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they do not conform to real world knowledge, decide which of the given conclusions/possibilities can be true on the basis of the statements.

**Statements:**

1. Some toys are pianos.

2. Some pianos are white.

3. All white are guitars.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some white are toys.

II. Some guitars are toys.

III. Some guitars are pianos.

options.text: Only conclusion I and II are true

solution:
Given Statements:

1. Some toys are pianos.

2. Some pianos are white.

3. All white are guitars.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/72acef826696ca4e4203cc958bb0263996e0c7982da793bd88c092048256ed40.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some white are toys - False (Because, No definite relation given between White and Toys, So, it can be possible only).

II. Some guitars are toys - False (Because, No definite relation given between guitars and Toys, So, it can be possible only).

III Some guitars are pianos - True (Because, those part of guitars which is white will also pianos).

So, Only conclusion III is true.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".
